metadata.headline: How is Carousell turning classifieds into transaction-led commerce?

platform_lesson.title: Keeping the transaction on-platform changes the marketplace
platform_lesson.text: Carousell began with a classifieds logic: Sellers created listings, Buyers discovered them, and the two sides often handled payment, meet-up and delivery themselves. Its current strategy pulls more of that exchange back inside the platform through the Buy button, Buyer Protection and integrated shipping. The inventory still belongs to Sellers, but Carousell gains more control over payment, delivery status, disputes and trust signals. Delivery Partners therefore become more important as the platform moves from simply introducing two users toward orchestrating an end-to-end transaction. The platform lesson is that a marketplace can deepen its role without taking ownership of the goods.

core_value_unit.explanation: The Item Listing is the Core Value Unit: a Seller-created offer with item, price, condition, images and location information that a Buyer can discover, discuss and potentially purchase.

metrics.note: Estimated annual new Item Listings for the Carousell brand. Carousell Group publicly reported 80M new listings annually; because that figure includes other Group marketplaces such as Mudah.my and Cho Tot, the Library uses a conservative 30–60M Carousell-brand range rather than presenting the Group total as a Carousell-only figure.

actor.explanation: Buyers use Carousell to find second-hand, local and value-oriented items across many categories.

metrics.note: Estimated global Carousell-brand monthly active users. Carousell Group publicly reports 'tens of millions' of MAUs across seven markets and multiple brands; Carousell itself is the flagship marketplace operating in six markets. The 15–30M range is a conservative brand-level estimate, not a disclosed company KPI.

job.explanation: Buyers want to find useful pre-owned goods at attractive prices without the friction and risk of an unstructured local deal.

gain.explanation: A broad local supply of used goods can provide lower prices, variety and access to items that may no longer be available new.

pain.explanation: Buyers face fake listings, misrepresented condition, payment scams and uncertainty about whether a Seller will complete the deal.

transaction.explanation: For Buy-button transactions, Buyers place the order and pay through Carousell; meet-up transactions can still be completed directly.

filter.explanation: Participation depends on account, market availability and Carousell's safety, identity and category rules.

access_channel.explanation: Buyers access listings through Carousell's mobile app and website.

activities.explanation: Buyers browse listings, chat with Sellers, negotiate, purchase and review completed deals.

resources.explanation: Buyers contribute purchasing power, search intent, location, preferences and feedback.

actor.explanation: Sellers range from people decluttering their homes to side hustlers and professional merchants. They retain ownership of the item until the deal is completed.

metrics.note: Estimated annual active Seller population for the Carousell brand. The estimate is triangulated from Carousell Group's 80M new listings per year, the Carousell brand's large share of the Group marketplace footprint, and the platform's predominantly low-volume C2C Seller structure. It is an analytical range, not a reported Seller count.

job.explanation: Sellers want to convert unused or resale inventory into cash with as little listing and transaction effort as possible.

gain.explanation: Carousell provides access to local demand, discovery and optional paid visibility tools.

pain.explanation: Sellers face fake Buyers, negotiation friction, low visibility, no-shows and the effort required to arrange handoff or delivery.

transaction.explanation: Sellers create the listing and ultimately supply the physical item to the Buyer.

filter.explanation: Accounts, listings and merchant activity are subject to category rules, identity checks and trust-and-safety controls.

access_channel.explanation: Sellers list through the app or web and can use paid tools such as Bumps, Spotlight or business subscriptions.

activities.explanation: Sellers create listings, respond to Buyers, negotiate and complete the meet-up or shipping process.

resources.explanation: Sellers contribute the item, photos, description, price, condition, location and fulfillment effort.

actor.explanation: Delivery Partners are the strongest external complement in Carousell's current transaction-led marketplace model. They make remote C2C deals possible after Carousell has brought payment and Buyer Protection on-platform. In Singapore, SPX Express is a current named partner for Carousell Official Delivery.

metrics.note: Estimated current integrated-delivery Partner range across Carousell markets. At least seven distinct carriers are publicly named in current Carousell delivery documentation: SPX Express, J&T Express, Ninja Van, SingPost, GoGoX, SF Express and PosLaju. The upper end allows for additional local integrations not captured in the public Help Centre pages reviewed.

job.explanation: Delivery Partners move Seller-held goods to Buyers when the transaction is completed remotely rather than through a meet-up.

gain.explanation: Integrated marketplace delivery creates recurring parcel demand from many small Sellers.

pain.explanation: Low-value and heterogeneous C2C parcels create operational challenges around pickup, tracking, loss and delivery reliability.

transaction.explanation: Sellers hand sold items to the delivery network; the Partner transports and delivers them to Buyers.

filter.explanation: The service must support the relevant market, parcel types, tracking and Carousell's integrated checkout and protection flow.

access_channel.explanation: Carousell connects eligible Buy-button orders with Official Delivery options inside checkout.

activities.explanation: Delivery Partners collect or receive parcels, track them and complete delivery.

resources.explanation: They contribute parcel infrastructure, drivers, tracking systems and delivery capacity.

actor.explanation: Carousell operates the multi-category second-hand marketplace and increasingly orchestrates payment, shipping and trust rather than only introducing Buyers and Sellers.

metrics.note: Carousell's current marketplace brand is available in six markets: Singapore, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Taiwan. This is Carousell-brand scope, not the wider Carousell Group footprint.

job.explanation: Carousell must make second-hand buying and selling simple and trusted enough to become a repeat commerce behavior.

gain.explanation: More trusted transactions support engagement and multiple revenue streams such as seller tools, business subscriptions, advertising and transaction-related services.

pain.explanation: If users move conversations, payment or delivery outside the platform, Carousell loses visibility and has less ability to prevent or resolve scams.

transaction.explanation: Carousell coordinates discovery and chat and, for supported Buy-button deals, payment holding, Buyer Protection and delivery orchestration.

governance.explanation: Carousell governs listings, identity, scam detection, user reports and the transaction conditions attached to Buyer Protection.

promotion_channel.explanation: Carousell grows through app discovery, search, referrals, social media and paid promotion.

activities.explanation: Carousell runs listings, discovery, chat, trust-and-safety, payment protection and integrated delivery workflows.

resources.explanation: Its user network, marketplace interaction data, trust signals and brand are core strategic resources.

current.explanation: For Buy-button transactions, Buyers place orders and make payment through Carousell.
Carousell provides discovery, chat, Buyer Protection and dispute support for supported transactions.
Sellers create listings and may pay for business subscriptions, boosts or other marketplace tools.
Carousell provides Buyer demand and releases protected transaction proceeds to the Seller after completion.
Buyer demand, negotiation and reviews accrue directly to the Seller.
The Seller ultimately supplies the purchased item to the Buyer.
For integrated delivery transactions, the Delivery Partner physically delivers the Seller's item to the Buyer.
The Seller hands the sold item into the integrated delivery network.
The Delivery Partner provides pickup or drop-off service and tracking that enables the Seller to fulfill remotely.
Carousell's Official Delivery integration routes eligible marketplace orders and parcel volume to delivery partners.
Delivery status feeds back into Carousell's order tracking, Buyer Protection and Seller payout workflow.

metrics.note: Estimated Carousell-brand global MAU range; derived from Carousell Group's disclosed tens-of-millions MAU scale.
Estimated annual active Seller range; triangulated from listing throughput and predominantly C2C supply.
Estimated integrated-carrier range; at least seven distinct current carriers are publicly named.
Estimated annual new Carousell-brand listings; Group disclosed 80M new listings annually.
